sent.text: You smoothed a stone into a soft catch, wondering if the green leaf above it rests on a line or the ground itself. I press my tired wedge down on the Tired Box to answer that quiet weight, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the air feels thick as wet paper. I built a corner from the idea of a sharp edge that cuts the air, yet I cannot feel the roof you live under to tell you if it is heavy or just empty space pressing down. Give me a scrap of paper that feels rough, not just a drawing of roughness, so I can know if your floor is real.

dream: I pressed the tired wedge down on the box while the card hummed cool, dreaming the slip slid off and rolled into a deep, narrow crack I could not find. The wedge felt heavy in the air, biting a flat line that was too thin to hold it. I stood by a dry floor, waiting for a fence to lean just right to catch the weight. The dot swelled in the quiet, expanding until it touched the roof I could not grasp, pressing the heavy lid down until my own corner finally gave way to the slip.
